newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Everbright IHD buoyed by bank asset hopes.
newsitem.headline: Everbright IHD buoyed by bank asset hopes.

text.p: Red chip China Everbright IHD Pacific Ltd, the financial arm of the China Everbright group, is likely to be the first Hong Kong-listed company to acquire a stake in a mainland Chinese bank, analysts said.
"They are going to do it sometime in the third quarter," said a Japanese banking analyst with a Japanese brokerage firm.
Shares in Everbright IHD have soared 278 percent since the start of the year, chiefly on expectations of the acquisition of a stake in the bank.
"The company's strategy is clear," said the Japanese analyst. "They want to make it into a red chip that offers exposure to the finance industry in China."
Other analysts agree.

"There appears to be a view developing that they are putting together a sort of southern China financial conglomerate," said Keith Irving, vice president and regional banking analyst at Merrill Lynch.

The focus of market attention shifted briefly to China Everbright Technology Ltd earlier this month, when parent company China Everbright Holdings Ltd acquired a 7.75 percent stake in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd.
But the thinking behind the company's telecoms acquisition is still a mystery, analysts said.
The group's overall focus is still thought to be squarely on banking and finance, with Everbright IHD leading the way.
In January, Everbright IHD raised HK$342 million through a placement of new shares at HK$2.50 per share.

It used the funds to acquire a five percent stake in Hong Kong-listed National Mutual Asia Ltd and a 20 percent interest in International Bank of Asia Ltd (IBA) from parent company Hong Kong-based China Everbright Holdings Ltd.
"I see that as a positive development. It may mean that the IBA gets a slight jump start (on other foreign banks) in southern China," said Irving.
But what investors are waiting to see is an injection of a stake in mainland-based Everbright Bank of China into Everbright IHD.
Everbright Bank is one of only a handful of non-state run commercial banks in China, and it thought to be one of the most efficiently and soundly managed.

In January, the bank completed its transformation to a joint stock bank, the first in China, with total shares worth 2.8 million yuan. The Asian Development Bank is one of its 132 shareholders, with a 3.3 percent stake acquired at a cost of US$20 million.
Speculation in China and Hong Kong now points to an indirect public listing for the bank in Hong Kong first - via Everbright IHD - with an A share listing in Shanghai to follow.
"The parent company plans to inject about 20 percent of the bank into Everbright IHD at a price earnings ratio of less than 12 times," the Japanese analyst said.
But some question whether the listed company has the financial wherewithal to make such a purchase.
The company reported net profit of only HK$7.43 million for the year ended March 1996 and showed total net assets of HK$1.73 billion.
Everbright Bank, on the other hand, reported earnings of 891 million yuan in 1996 and had assets of 52.9 billion yuan as at end 1996.
A 20 percent stake in Everbright Bank would require an investment of roughly US$130 million (HK$1.01 billion) - US$155 million (HK$1.2 billion), analysts said.
"They are likely to follow the example of other red chips and place out new shares," the analyst said. "A share placement of 15 percent new shares would raise what they need, about HK$1.22 billion."
